startup.name: Ossus
startup.description: AI-native operating system for school and public libraries that saves librarians time on cataloging and routine tasks. Customers are libraries and school districts. Three person team.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already accepted, so this is a note. A random applicant starts near 1 percent. A small team, an unusual market with little venture precedent and no stated traction hold the estimate down, while a clear user and a technical product keep it above the base.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because libraries are a small, budget constrained, slow buying market with entrenched vendors, and the pitch gives no revenue or pilots. Reviewers may doubt that a three person team can displace Follett's Destiny and still reach a venture sized outcome.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed stalls if investors conclude libraries are too small and slow, with school budgets cut and procurement by district. Revenue per library is low, so a venture sized outcome needs thousands of customers. Openbase and other niche tooling companies in the data raised little and stopped. A pivot to broader cultural institutions would need to happen quickly.

ladder.why_it_fails: The company stops before a Series C because the library market is small and consolidated into a few vendors, so growth beyond Series B is more likely to end in a sale to an incumbent like Follett or Clarivate than in a large independent round.

outcomes.why_it_fails: A venture sized outcome is unlikely because the market is small and prices are low. Most failure paths are a stall once the seed money runs out without district contracts, or a small acquisition by an incumbent library vendor. Most analogs in the cohort that did not reach a later round also lacked a repeatable paying customer base, and exits in this category tend to be small.

killers.risk: Small and slow public sector market with low prices
killers.evidence: Library budgets are limited, buying runs through districts and Follett's Destiny already dominates school libraries.
killers.mitigation: Sell to public library systems with larger budgets first and price on time saved.

killers.risk: Incumbents add AI to existing systems
killers.evidence: Destiny AI is already described by reviewers and Clarivate keeps releasing updates to Sierra.
killers.mitigation: Be a layer that works with existing catalogs rather than replacing them.

killers.evidence: Niche vertical tools in the data raised small seeds and stopped when revenue stayed flat.
killers.mitigation: Expand to museums, archives and universities early.

competition_now.name: Follett Destiny
competition_now.what: Library manager that leads the school library market, now with an AI assistant.
competition_now.traction: Market share reported at five times the next rival in a 2019 report.

technical_complexity.rationale: Cataloging, search and workflow automation with current language models are within reach of a three person team in months. The harder part is integrating with entrenched library systems and meeting school data privacy rules.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents already ship AI assistants and own the customer relationships, so they could match the main features within a year, though they move slowly.

evidence.claim: School and public libraries already pay for library systems, and vendors are adding AI features, so spend exists but is modest.

roadmap.goal: Show paid library customers beyond pilots.
actions: Sign ten paying libraries with annual contracts.
roadmap.proof: Ten paid sites and a reference district.

actions: Win a district or consortium with many libraries.

pros.evidence: Librarians do tedious cataloging and routine tasks that language models handle well.
The product is software on existing models, buildable by a small team.

brand.name: Ossus
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Ossus" --era 2022+ : kind invented_or_proper, alive 92.7 percent, n=1826
brand.rationale: Ossus is short and invented, like many YC names, but it does not signal libraries or culture. Public sector buyers rely on references and price, so the name will not move the outcome much.

narrative.headline: A real but small market for a tiny team, with a coin flip on a seed and a hard road to Series A.
narrative.general_summary: Ossus builds an AI native operating system for school and public libraries. Librarians do tedious work that models can automate, and the product is technically simple. The problem is the market: budgets are small, buying is slow, Follett's Destiny dominates school libraries and is adding AI, and the three person team has no stated traction. A seed larger than the YC check within a year is possible but below the B2B cohort rate, and a venture sized outcome would need expansion to museums and other cultural institutions. About half of simulated paths stall, and most of the rest end in a small sale.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05 using only the batch description.
Anchors use B2B cohorts because no library or culture cohort exists.
